hero.intro_en: Write a professional email to your manager that explains the ROI of a marketing campaign in simple terms. You practice connecting actions to financial results, the language of business in the U.S.
hero.intro_es: Escribe un correo profesional a tu jefe que explique el ROI de una campaña de marketing en términos simples. Practicas conectar acciones con resultados financieros: el lenguaje de los negocios en EE. UU.

hint.en: Your bottom line in one sentence.
hint.es: Tu conclusión principal en una oración.

parts.example: Here's a quick update: the campaign was a success.
phrases: Here's a quick update on the [name] campaign.
Good news: the campaign exceeded our goal.
In short, the campaign more than paid for itself.

hint.en: Cost, sales and the ROI, with numbers.
hint.es: Costo, ventas y ROI, con números.

parts.example: We spent $5,000 and brought in $12,500 in new sales…
phrases: We invested $[cost] and generated $[sales] in new sales.
That's a return of [X]% on our investment.
For every dollar we spent, we brought in $[X].

hint.es: Resalta con claridad lo que salió bien.

phrases: This was our best-performing campaign this year.

parts.en: An idea for the next campaign
parts.es: Una idea para la próxima campaña

hint.en: One suggestion based on this success.
hint.es: Una sugerencia basada en este éxito.

parts.example: For the next campaign, I suggest…
phrases: For the next campaign, I suggest we [idea].
Based on these results, I recommend investing more in [channel].
I'd like to test [idea] with a small budget first.

parts.example: I'm happy to share the full numbers… Best regards,
phrases: I'm happy to walk you through the numbers.
Let me know if you have any questions.

rules.d_en: Main result first, short sentences, no jargon.
rules.d_es: Resultado principal primero, oraciones cortas, sin tecnicismos.

rules.d_en: Cost, sales and ROI, rounded and easy to read.
rules.d_es: Costo, ventas y ROI, redondeados y fáciles de leer.

rules.d_en: Subject line, paragraph spacing, no emojis.
rules.d_es: Línea de asunto, párrafos separados, sin emojis.

example.subject: Email campaign results: 150% ROI
paragraphs: Here's a quick update on our spring email campaign: it was a success, and it more than paid for itself.
We spent $5,000 and brought in $12,500 in new sales. In simple terms, that's a return on investment of 150%: for every dollar we spent, we got back $2.50.
The strongest results came from our loyalty customers, and we also gained 300 new subscribers who can buy from us again. It was our best-performing campaign this year.
For the next campaign, I suggest we send a special offer to these new subscribers and test it with a small budget first.
I'm happy to walk you through the full numbers at our meeting on Thursday. Please let me know if you have any questions.

original.title: Explaining ROI in an Email
original.body_en:
✍️ Writing Task

Title: Explaining ROI in an Email
Time: 1–2 hours

Scenario:
You are in marketing and ran a campaign that cost $8,000. The campaign brought in $24,000 in new sales. Your manager asks for an update.

Your Task: Write a professional email (120–150 words) to your manager that:

Explains the ROI in simple terms.

Highlights the positive results clearly.

Suggests one idea for the next campaign based on this success.

Why This Matters:
Showing you can connect actions to financial results proves you understand the language of business—something U.S. employers value highly.
original.body_es:
✍️ Tarea de Escritura

Título: Explicando el ROI en un Correo Electrónico
Tiempo: 1–2 horas

Escenario:
Estás en marketing y realizaste una campaña que costó $8,000. La campaña generó $24,000 en nuevas ventas. Tu gerente solicita una actualización.

Tu tarea: Escribe un correo electrónico profesional (120–150 palabras) a tu gerente que:

Explique el ROI en términos simples.

Resalte claramente los resultados positivos.

Sugiera una idea para la próxima campaña basada en este éxito.

Por qué es importante:
Demostrar que puedes conectar acciones con resultados financieros prueba que entiendes el lenguaje de los negocios, algo que los empleadores en EE. UU. valoran mucho.
